title: Douglas v. Deutsche Bank National Trust Co., No. 24-CV-1099, Published Order

reading.body:
On the reporting available, this is a case of a model asserting something false as fact and that assertion reaching a court. A District of Columbia court faulted lawyers for a Deutsche Bank subsidiary over an AI hallucination, according to the Reuters headline. The failure sits at the point where generated text entered a legal filing, a document whose contents are weighed by a tribunal.

Catching it would have taken a person checking the generated material against the underlying record before the filing was submitted. Nothing in the reporting indicates that check happened. The order is published under the case name Douglas v. Deutsche Bank National Trust Co., No. 24-CV-1099.

What was hallucinated, what the court's reasoning was, and whether any penalty followed are not established here. The text of the order was not readable in the material supplied, so the account rests on the headline alone. A court faulting the lawyers is a finding by that court, and the facts it relied on are not visible in these sources.
